customManagers.description: The Go analyzers the check runner shells out to are pinned as `@vX.Y.Z` string literals inside `EnsureGoTool(...)` calls, so no manager sees them. They went stale silently until a Go 1.27 bump broke CI: staticcheck 2026.1 can't decode Go 1.27 export data, and the toolchain PR had no way to know the pin needed to move with it. `packageName` captures the module root (`honnef.co/go/tools`) because the goproxy 404s on a package path (`honnef.co/go/tools/cmd/staticcheck`), while `depName` keeps the full install path so `autoReplaceStringTemplate` can write the line back verbatim.

packageRules.description: The check runner's Go analyzers land on their own, for the same reason the linters below do: an analyzer bump re-flags tracked source across every Go module, which is noise to review mixed in with dependency changes. `go.uber.org/nilaway` publishes no tags, so its pseudo-version pin gets no PRs; move it by hand when it matters.

Default lane for non-major updates. Split per app below, because one repo-wide batch pooled five unrelated breakages (a genai field, a new stylelint rule, an oxfmt reformat, two typecheck breaks) into a single 2,300-line PR that couldn't be reviewed or bisected. Per-app groups stay small enough to fix in one sitting.

Desktop app deps, Rust and JS together (a specta bump regenerates bindings.ts, so they have to land as one). Dashboard-only, because a desktop PR can never go green on its own: every lockfile touch leaves `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` stale, and the check only REGENERATES on a local run (`docs/guides/update-dependencies.md`). Renovate can't run that regeneration, since `postUpgradeTasks` needs a self-hosted `allowedCommands`. On top of that, semver-minor Rust crates break compilation for real (russh 0.63 changed the `check_server_key` signature and broke `cmdr-sftp`), which no bot fixes. Both attempted PRs failed: #41 closed, #97 red for five days. So Renovate keeps discovering versions and lists them on the Dependency Dashboard; a human ticks the box, or the weekly `/weekly-upgrades` pass does the whole batch in a worktree.
Worker + dashboard deps: both are Cloudflare-targeted and share wrangler.
Linters and formatters land on their own: a version bump here rewrites or re-flags tracked files across every app, which is noise to review mixed in with real dependency changes.

Docker images, pinned by digest for Scorecard's Pinned-Dependencies (`FROM image:tag@sha256:...`), so a tag that upstream re-points can't change what we build. Every digest refresh and non-major tag bump across all Dockerfiles and compose files lands as one weekly PR that automerges on green CI, overriding the per-app groups above (the desktop one would otherwise hold the test-fixture images for dashboard approval). Majors still go through the dashboard rule below. The top-level `dockerfile` / `docker-compose` blocks give these two managers their own `ignorePaths`, without `**/test/**`, since most images are test fixtures. The listmonk image's tag is an ARG, which Renovate can't read: `infra/listmonk/README.md` § Updates.
The fixture compose files name their locally built images (`cmdr-sftp-fixture:latest` and friends); no registry has them.

Majors, dashboard-only for the same reason as the desktop group: a major needs code changes, so an unattended PR just sits red and mails about it (#61, TypeScript v7, sat red for ten days). Renovate still tracks what's available; `/weekly-upgrades` decides which ones to take.
schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: Security patches get immediate PRs, auto-merge
First-party crates (David's own). Stricter pre-release gate than the 3-day window protects against; bypass so cmdr pulls fixes immediately.

The specta trio stays on rc.24 / 0.0.11. rc.25 types every plain `f32`/`f64` as `number | null`. On return values that's defensible (serde_json renders NaN/Infinity as null), but it does the same to PARAMETERS, where it's wrong: `viewer_get_lines(target_value: f64)` and the four `media_index_*_threshold` commands take non-Option floats and serde rejects a JSON null for them. Adopting it trades a latent, never-observed hazard for a live one, plus ~25 sites of null-handling. Rationale: `apps/desktop/src-tauri/DETAILS.md` § Number types over IPC. Re-evaluate on the next rc; bump all three together or not at all.

`cookie` stays below 2.0: that release renamed the whole API, and `@sveltejs/kit`'s runtime still imports the 0.x/1.x names, so 2.x breaks the SvelteKit build. Raise the ceiling only once Kit uses the 2.x names. The override and the full rationale live in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.
The SMB benchmark harness pins sspi and smb-rpc in lockstep with smb 0.11's internal pins; independent bumps can never resolve, so leave the whole harness alone.
